transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately I can’t seem to focus on my work the way I used to—my mind keeps drifting to everything that could go wrong, and I have to reread the same documents over and over. As a real estate broker, I deal with important contracts daily, and this is starting to make me very concerned about my work.
Beyond these worries, have you lost interest in activities you usually enjoy, or have you been feeling a persistent sense of sadness or emptiness lately?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or empty, and I haven't lost interest in the things I love. It's just that I've been turning down social invitations lately because I feel too exhausted and on edge to actually be present with my friends. I still want to be there, but my mind is just too overwhelmed right now.
Do you ever experience sudden, intense surges of fear or physical discomfort—such as a racing heart, dizziness, or shortness of breath—that reach a peak within minutes?

No, I don't really experience those sudden, intense surges of panic that peak out of nowhere. For me, it's more of a constant, slow-burning worry that's always there, although I do sometimes wake up early in the morning with my heart racing.
Besides the racing heart when you wake up, have you noticed persistent physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, or feeling easily fatigued throughout the day?

Yes, absolutely. By the end of the day, my shoulders and neck feel like concrete, and I clench my jaw so tightly during drives that I get headaches and my dentist says I'm grinding my teeth. I also feel constantly exhausted and worn down during the day because my sleep has been so poor.
Over the past six months, would you say you have spent more days worrying than not about a variety of different things, such as your work, your health, or your daily responsibilities?

Yes, I've been worrying almost every single day for over a year now, which is well over six months. My worries aren't limited to just one thing; they constantly chain together, covering my real estate work, my mortgage, health insurance, and even how my niece is doing at college. It really feels like my mind is always running worst-case scenarios about everything.

The absence of episodic panic attacks and the lack of depressive symptoms further solidify this focus.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with excessive, uncontrollable worry regarding multiple domains (work, finances, health, family) persisting for over a year, accompanied by physical symptoms of tension (muscle tightness, jaw clenching, fatigue, sleep disturbance), consistent with Generalized Anxiety Disorder.
